claim: The Ministry of Textiles (28 Dec 2016) said Rs 200 crore was sanctioned to Tamil Nadu for 18 CETPs of the Tirupur dyeing industry, as an interest-free loan to be converted into a grant on performance, and that 450 units had set up 18 ZLD-enabled CETPs at a total cost of Rs 1,013 crore.

evidence.quote: Ministry of Finance has sanctioned Rs 200.00 Crores to the State Government of Tamil Nadu for the 18 CETPs as an interest free loan to be converted into grant based on the performance of the CETPs.
More than 450 dyeing units in Tirupur Dyeing Industry had collectively set up 18 ZLD enabled Common Effluent plants (CETPs) with a total cost of Rs 1013.00 cr.

notes: Primary release; upgrades C180, which was read only as quoted by the Economic Times.

claim: The same 2016 release called the Tirupur ZLD CETPs 'the first ever Zero Liquid Discharge (ZLD) projects in the country' and said the dyeing industry 'was on the verge of closure due to severe financial crisis'.

evidence.quote: The Government of India has sanctioned Rs 200.00 Crores to the Tirupur Dyeing industry who was on the verge of closure due to severe financial crisis on account of their huge investments in the first ever Zero Liquid Discharge (ZLD) projects in the country.

notes: Government's own claim of 'first'; attribute, do not say it as fact.

claim: In Dec 2016 the Ministry of Textiles said Tirupur provides employment to over 5 lakh persons and 'contributes 22% of the total garment export of the country'.

evidence.quote: Tirupur is a hub of the textile processing and knitting industry providing employment to over 5 lakh persons and contributes 22% of the total garment export of the country.

notes: Official share, a different base (all garment exports) from the knitwear-share figures C066-C080. Use only dated and attributed; it undercuts any '90% of India's garment exports' reading.

claim: The Ministry of Textiles' written reply (11 Aug 2026, PIB) lists Tiruppur first among 548 exporting districts in 2025-26 with Rs 38,677 crore of textiles and readymade garments including handicrafts (DGCIS provisional, rounded).

evidence.quote: The top ten textile and readymade garment exporting districts, including handicrafts, during 2025–26 were Tiruppur (₹38,677 crore), Gautam Buddha Nagar (₹21,095 crore), Bengaluru Urban (₹16,205 crore)
Textile and readymade garments, including handicrafts, were exported from 548 districts across the country in 2025-26.

notes: Government figure for the district. Does not explain TEA's three FY26 figures (C076) but gives an official anchor for the district: use this one for FY26, labelled provisional.

claim: The Ministry's Dec 2025 reply gives Tamil Nadu's textile and apparel exports (incl. handicrafts) as USD 3,975.04 million (Apr-Sep 2024) and 4,078.06 million (Apr-Sep 2025), +2.6%, and says exports from Tirupur, Karur, Erode, Coimbatore and Salem together grew 11.4% in the same half-year.

evidence.quote: The total exports of Textiles & Apparel (incl handicrafts) from Tirupur, Karur, Erode, Coimbatore and Salem has shown a growth of 11.4% during the period Apr-Sep 2025 compared to corresponding period of previous year.
Total T&A including Handicrafts 3,975.04 4,078.06 2.6%

notes: The two figures sit awkwardly together (a five-district cluster up 11.4% inside a state up 2.6%); the reply does not explain this. Do not narrate either as Tiruppur-only.

claim: The Supreme Court's judgment of 6 Oct 2009 records that the Noyyal River Ayacutdars Protection Association's public interest litigation was Writ Petition 29791 of 2003, decided by the Madras High Court on 22 Dec 2006, and that dyeing and bleaching units at 'Tirupur area' were discharging effluents into the Noyyal, making its water unfit for irrigation or drinking and affecting the Orthapalayam reservoir.

evidence.quote: These appeals have been filed against the Judgment and Order dated 22.12.2006 of the Madras High Court in writ petition no. 29791 of 2003
discharging the industrial effluents into the Noyyal river which created water pollution to the extent, that the water of the river was neither fit for irrigation nor potable.

notes: Court text (Indian Kanoon copy of the SC judgment, Bench K.G. Balakrishnan, B.S. Chauhan; Dr B.S. Chauhan J. writing), primary for what the court recorded. Confirms 2003 filing for this petition; court spells the dam 'Orthapalayam' in one place and 'Orathapalayam' in another.

claim: The same judgment records the High Court's order: CETPs pay a fine of six, eight and ten paise per litre in successive periods up to 31 Jul 2007, and if they fail to achieve ZLD on or before 31 Jul 2007 the Pollution Control Board shall direct closure of the CETPs and member units and disconnect their power.

evidence.quote: In any event, if the CETPs or any of them fail to achieve the ZLD on or before 31st July, 2007, the Pollution Control Board shall forthwith direct closure of such CETPs and the Member Units and also disconnect the power supply to such defaulting CETP and the Member Units.
at the rate of eight paise per litre from Ist April, 2007 to 31st May, 2007; and at the rate of ten paise per litre from 1st June, 2007 to 31st July, 2007.

notes: Primary text for C170; replaces its trade-press source. The Supreme Court stayed only the closure on 31 Jul 2007 and extended the stay 'from time to time'.

claim: The Supreme Court records that the dyeing units' association had earlier been before the High Court in Writ Petition 1649 of 1996 (Karur Taluk Noyyal Canal Agriculturists Association), disposed of on 26 Feb 1998 on a joint memorandum of understanding to implement pollution control and pay damages, so Noyyal pollution litigation predates the 2003 petition.

evidence.quote: A similar issue i.e. menace of pollution had also earlier been raised by another association namely Karur Taluk Noyyal Canal Agriculturists Association by filing writ petition(c) no. 1649 of 1996 before the Madras High Court.
The High Court disposed of the said petition vide judgment and order dated 26.2.1998 on the basis of joint Memo of Understanding filed by all the contesting parties

notes: Corrects the framing of C169 (spine): 'fought polluters since 2003' is true of the Ayacutdars Association's own petition, but court action over the same pollution is on record from 1996. Say 'since 2003' only for that association.
replaces: C169 (qualifies: Ayacutdars Association petition 2003; earlier Karur association case 1996-98)

claim: The Coimbatore District Gazetteer (1966) describes Tiruppur as a railway station about twenty-six miles from Coimbatore, headquarters of its taluk, with population 52,479 (census year not given at that line; the volume cites the 1951 census elsewhere).

evidence.quote: Tiruppur (Population 52,479), a railway station about twenty-six miles from Coimbatore, is the headquarters of the taluk.

notes: 26 miles x 1.609344 = 41.8 km (calculated); agrees roughly with the measured straight line 42.6 km (C200); the gazetteer does not say whether road, rail or straight. Town size before the boom: 52,479, a small town. Census year to be confirmed before narrating the number.

claim: The 1966 gazetteer says merchants from all mill centres in the country visit Tiruppur in the season to buy the high-reputation Cambodia cotton of Avanashi taluk.

evidence.quote: merchants from all mill centres in the country visit Tiruppur to buy this first class cotton in the season.

notes: Cotton-trade town before hosiery; the gazetteer is a government compilation (P3, period record, 1966).

claim: The 1966 gazetteer records that the cotton regulated market, set up under the Madras Commercial Crop Markets Act of 1933, originally (1936) dealt only with cotton and only within the limits of the Tiruppur municipality; it extended to the whole district in 1950.

evidence.quote: Originally (in 1936) it dealt only with cotton, confining its operation only to the area within the limits of the Tiruppur municipality.

notes: Tiruppur was the first place where the district's cotton market was regulated (1936).

claim: The 1966 gazetteer records labour unrest in Tiruppur in the late 1940s: strikes began in January 1947 in the Asher and Dhanalakshmi Mills, Tiruppur, and grew into a district-wide mill strike of over 35,000 workers; a later passage says the Communists stirred up strikes 'in a knitting factory at Tiruppur'.

evidence.quote: These strikes began early in January in the Asher and Dhanalakshmi Mills, Tiruppur
stirred up strikes in the Somasundara and Kaleswara Mills, Coimbatore, and in a knitting factory at Tiruppur.

notes: The earliest dated record found of a union dispute at a Tiruppur knitting factory (late 1940s; the passage follows the 1947-48 fortnightly reports, exact date not given). Colonial/government record: written from an anti-Communist viewpoint (the gazetteer says strikers 'attacked all loyal workers'); attribute. Consistent with Subbarayan (father at Dhanalakshmi mill, AITUC) in S06.

claim: The 1966 gazetteer does not describe Tiruppur as a hosiery or banian centre: the only knitting references are a count of '10 knitting mills' among large-scale industries of the whole district and the 1940s strike line; the cottage-industry section names Tiruppur for khadi spinning and weaving, dyeing, printing and brass vessels.

evidence.quote: The rest of the large scale industries consist of 141 cotton ginning and pressing establishments, 10 knitting mills, 16 textile dyeing and printing works
As regards khader cloths, they are produced from spun yarn in and around Tiruppur where a large number of looms are engaged in weaving them.

notes: Absence claim: searched the full text for hosier*, banian, banyan, knitting, undergarment. 10 knitting mills in the whole district in the gazetteer's late-1950s/60s data. Consistent with a knitwear town that was still small in 1960 (C035: 230 firms) but note the gazetteer does not name Tiruppur's units. Do not say 'the gazetteer ignores hosiery'; say 'the gazetteer counts 10 knitting mills for the whole district'.

claim: The 1887 Manual of the Coimbatore District records steam cotton presses at Coimbatore, Palladam and Tirupur, and calls Tirupur 'a busy railway station, whence a great deal of cotton is despatched'.

evidence.quote: There are steam-cotton presses at Coimbatore, Palladam and Tirupur, and hand-presses at Erode and Palladam.
Tirupur, a busy railway station, whence a great deal of cotton is despatched

notes: Colonial administrative manual (1887 per archive.org catalogue; the scanned title page is not in the text layer): an interested record. Cotton and railway at Tirupur are about 50 years before the first hosiery unit.

claim: A Madras Agricultural Journal study of the Tirupur cotton market (Vol 44, K. Sriraman) says Tirupur had 26 ginning factories, about 32 kapas commission merchants, about 2 lakh pothis (280 lb a pothi) of kapas arriving a year, a March-June season, and that Coimbatore, 'hardly within 30 miles', had 42 yarn and textile mills.

evidence.quote: There are 26 ginning factories at Tirupur and nearly 32 kapas commission merchants housed within the regulated market at Tirupur market the bulk of the arrivals.
Hardly within 30 miles from Tirupur is situated the Coimbatore town-the "Manchester of South India" which bustles with industry, having 42 yarn and textile, mills.

notes: Peer-reviewed journal, period study (pounds and pothis, so before metrication; the page gives no issue year, the journal's Vol 23 is 1935 so Vol 44 is most likely the mid-1950s, an inference only; the online posting date of 5 Nov 2023 is not the study date). Use 'a mid-twentieth-century study' unless the year is confirmed.

claim: A 1930s investigation of finance and marketing of cultivators' cotton at Tiruppur town was carried out in 1932 and 1933 with a scholarship from the Indian Central Cotton Committee (S.V. Duraiswami, Madras Agricultural Journal Vol 23).

evidence.quote: Investigations into the finance and marketing of cultivators cotton in Tirupur town and in two representative villages of the Indian were carried out by the authhor with the aid of a scholarship from the Indian Central Cotton Committee to 1932 and 1933

notes: Abstract only read; full text not opened. Shows Tiruppur was studied as a cotton-marketing town in 1932-33, the decade of the 1930s hosiery unit.

claim: Official spellings differ by year and department: 'Tiruppur' (1966 gazetteer; district page; Ministry of Textiles 2025 and 2026 releases), 'Tirupur' (1887 manual; Ministry of Textiles Dec 2016 release; the Supreme Court judgment 2009).

evidence.quote: Central Government sanctions of Rs 200.00 Crores for the Tirupur Dyeing Industry
Tiruppur (₹38,677 crore)

notes: For the voice: both spellings are said the same. Official current spelling is 'Tiruppur' (S37 district page and the 2025-26 Ministry releases). The Tamil-script spelling was not opened from a primary source in this sweep.
